### Added
- **The chart provisions Agent Substrate's snapshot store on CAPZ** (giantswarm/agent-platform#417, giantswarm/giantswarm#37756): `kagent.harness.snapshotStore.crossplane.provider: capz` renders, through the connectivity chart, the Azure storage `Account` (TLS-only, no public blob access, seven-day soft delete; never deleted by Crossplane, kept by Helm), the blob `Container` with a lifecycle `ManagementPolicy` (`capz.lifecycleDays`, 30 by default), a `UserAssignedIdentity` with a `FederatedIdentityCredential` against the cluster's OIDC issuer for the s3proxy ServiceAccount and a `RoleAssignment` (Storage Blob Data Contributor, scoped to the container; provider-kubernetes `Object`s bridge the identity's generated principalId, clientId and tenantId the way the Loki chart does), and the **s3proxy façade** (`kagent.harness.snapshotStore.s3proxy`): Substrate speaks S3 only, so a stateless two-replica `substrate-s3proxy` Deployment in the release namespace (the gsoci mirror of gaul/s3proxy, non-root on 8080 behind a Service on 80, a PodDisruptionBudget, network policies in both flavours admitting only atelet and ate-api-server, Substrate's egress to it next to the bundled store's) translates `aws-v4` — a per-installation key pair generated once and kept, the Secret `substrate-s3proxy` in the release namespace and in `ate-system` — to `azureblob` as the identity (`DefaultAzureCredential`, `azure.workload.identity/use`). The meta chart derives `kagent.harness.snapshotLocation` = `s3://<capz.containerName>/<prefix>` and hands the substrate release `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`, `AWS_S3_USE_PATH_STYLE`, `AWS_REGION` and the key pair on `atelet.extraEnv` and `ateApiServer.extraEnv` next to an installation's own entries. The façade also runs alone (`s3proxy.enabled: true`, the Crossplane block off) in front of an account provisioned by hand or a lab's Azurite (`s3proxy.azure.*`, an account key). Guards: the provider, each provider's inputs, the account name's shape, the endpoint's scheme, the bundled store on, an own S3 variable, a disagreeing `snapshotLocation` or `s3proxy.azure.*`. Off and `aws` render byte-identically to 4.9.x; `make verify-substrate-store` extended, `ci/test-substrate-store-capz-values.yaml`, `tests/verify-components.py` pins the façade's image to gsoci and the BOM; `hack/agentlab/` carries the lab's Azurite fixture and overlay. Measured in agentlab against Azurite: one 2 GiB object, in-cluster aws-cli: PUT 9.8 s (209 MB/s), GET 7.4 s (276 MB/s) through the façade into Azurite, against PUT 5.8 s (356 MB/s), GET 3.0 s (684 MB/s) on the bundled RustFS — the façade's hop costs about 1.7× on writes and 2.5× on reads in the lab; an actor's golden snapshot restores from the store in ~0.24 s (manifest 11 ms, download 37 ms, restore 190 ms).
### Changed
- **The WorkerPool is one CPU feature set, not one architecture** (giantswarm/agent-platform#429): `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.template.nodeSelector` pinned the pool to `kubernetes.io/arch: amd64` and the values comment, the READMEs and UPGRADE.md said an actor's golden snapshot is architecture-specific. The constraint is narrower: the snapshot is a gVisor checkpoint, and gVisor restores it only on a host whose CPU offers every feature the checkpoint recorded — two amd64 nodes of different vendors are not compatible. On the first 4.x installation (2026-09-13) Karpenter had mixed AMD `c5a` and Intel `r6i` nodes under the pool; the `sre-agent` golden snapshot was taken on an AMD worker, every restore on the Intel worker failed `incompatible FeatureSet: missing features: cmp_legacy, cr8_legacy, sse4a, misalignsse, topoext, mmxext, fxsr_opt` (all AMD-only CPUID flags) every 30 s, and the portal turn surfaced as `actor "ai-…" request timed out` — the actor never recovers because it stays placed on that worker. The chart's default stays `kubernetes.io/arch: amd64` (the coarse case, and the only label every provider carries); the values comment, the chart README, the README's "Scheduling" paragraph and UPGRADE.md now name the feature-set constraint and the pin per provider: on CAPA the vendor `karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-cpu-manufacturer: amd|intel` (Karpenter consolidation may replace a node with another vendor's at any time) and, where a generation change must be ruled out too, the family `karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-family`; on CAPZ and the other providers the node pool (`giantswarm.io/machine-pool`) or `node.kubernetes.io/instance-type`; and the recognition recipe (the worker log line, `kubectl get nodes -L <the label>` showing two values under the pool). No render change. **Installations act**: a CAPA installation whose workers Karpenter provisions adds the vendor its golden snapshots were taken on to `kagent.substrateWorkerPool.template.nodeSelector` — the fleet template carries `karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-cpu-manufacturer: amd` for every CAPA installation on the 4.x line (shared-configs, `agentPlatform.workerPoolCpuManufacturer`), so a Giant Swarm installation acts only to tighten or to opt out. The durable fix is Substrate's — a restore placed only on a worker whose CPU covers the snapshot's feature set (giantswarm/giantswarm#37742 row 12).
